originalFindings.title: Correct response-label spelling 例外無し is rejected
originalFindings.claim: Both answer arrays accept only 例外なし and れいがいなし. 例外無し is the same defined no-exception label with the supported written form of なし. The instructions define labels and permit kana but do not impose an exact mixed-script spelling restriction.
originalFindings.impact: A semantically correct typed response can receive a false negative in both tasks.
originalFindings.minimalRemedy: Add 例外無し to both existing answer classes and handle the corresponding supported mixed-kana rendering れいがい無し consistently. Retain model buttons, target/SRS identities and group ownership; do not add spelling-only quiz buttons. Refresh lexical context fingerprints after the accepted-answer change.
evidence: Actual stored arrays are [例外なし, れいがいなし]; direct trim/NFKC membership checks reject 例外無し and れいがい無し.

S22: Shogakukan Digital Daijisen なし【無し】 senses 1-2 support absence and noun-compound attachment.

originalFindings.title: Three facets count repeated operations as two independent contexts
originalFindings.claim: Each of per-period, item-price and activity-duration has exactly two authored keys but the pair repeats the same assessed operation. Varied neighboring facets cannot supply its missing second context.

affectedFacets.analysis: Both instructions name the count and period, present count first, prescribe に and require period + に + count. Week/hour, 回/本 and supplied destination/arrival predicates change lexical material but not assembly or role mapping. The train subject is already outside the blank.
Both are この item は amount する and ask only main-predicate use. Supplied します versus しました is neither formed nor separately interpreted by the response; both select 価格 from the same relation.
Both use activity を duration します. Today versus every morning supplies different background, but the question does not assess plan versus habit. The same object/duration relation yields 活動時間.

originalFindings.impact: The local two-genuinely-distinct-context requirement is not met for three facets; 26 different strings cannot be used as proof of compliant transfer breadth.
originalFindings.minimalRemedy: Retain useful drills and identities, but revise at least one member of each affected facet to require a genuinely different relevant interpretation or assembly decision within the same answer class. If repeats remain, share their key and supply another genuine context. Renaming or merging keys alone is insufficient.
evidence: Complete prompts/instructions/answers and introduction-group member keys in the listed ranges.
docs\content-format.md:265-268: at least two distinct context keys per facet; near-duplicates share keys.
Approved work-item acceptance criterion: one answer class per facet, at least two genuinely distinct contexts, paired examples sharing keys.
Permitted reusable lessons require operation-sensitive counting and independent within-facet variation.
originalFindings.confidence: High for repeated operations; replacement contexts remain an editorial decision.

dispositions.title: All three affected facets now have genuinely different relevant operations

facetResolutions.actualDifference: The library task assembles an adverbial 一週間に二回. The train task requires 一時間に四本の before 電車, adding a genuine count-to-noun attachment decision rather than only changing period/counter nouns.
facetResolutions.formationAudit: The instructions specify the named rate frame and noun-modification operation but do not print the missing の or a whole answer. All four accepted written/kana realizations fit the complete sentence.
facetResolutions.wrongCompletionAudit: 一時間ごとに電車がこの駅に来ます is grammatical but loses the specified four-train count and requested count-to-noun link. Feedback identifies those task failures rather than banning the construction.
facetResolutions.articleRegressionCheck: The article explicitly retains the natural adverbial count arrangement as an alternative outside this named operation.
facetResolutions.levelReason: N4 frequency plus N5 noun-linking support.

facetResolutions.revisedPrompt: 「二千円した時計の修理に三十分かかりました。」→____
facetResolutions.actualDifference: The cup task classifies a main price predicate; the watch task selects inner した modifying 時計 while an actual outer かかりました expresses required repair time. Main-predicate-only classification now fails, so this is not merely tense substitution.
facetResolutions.instructionAudit: Identifying which predicate is queried supplies legitimate answer-independent scope, not the price response label.

branchAudit.価格: Selected inner monetary predicate attributes price to the watch.
branchAudit.必要量: The outer repair-time predicate does have this meaning, but it is not the selected predicate.
branchAudit.活動時間: Selected した is not ordinary activity duration; outer required time remains separate.

facetResolutions.lexicalAudit: 二千円, 時計, 修理 and 三十分 have appropriate readings/glosses; both した and かかりました remain protected.
facetResolutions.levelReason: N4 price/resource predicates plus N5 plain-past noun description.

facetResolutions.revisedPrompt: 「今朝、運動をした時間は五分でした。」→____
facetResolutions.actualDifference: The cleaning task uses adverbial duration with します; the revised task requires reading 運動をした modifying 時間 and 五分でした as a nominal quantity predication. This changes composition needed for interpretation, not just time adverbs or tense.
facetResolutions.branchAudit: All branches distinguish actual time spent on the named activity from monetary price or asserted required completion time. No claim of mandatory completion or noncompletion is introduced.
facetResolutions.lexicalAudit: 今朝 is this morning, not every morning; 時間 is neutral time, not an answer-revealing gloss; した is protected and でした is a function exclusion.
facetResolutions.stableIdQualification: The retained exercise ID contains habitual but learner-visible content no longer makes the old habitual claim. Stable identity is intentional, not a defect.
facetResolutions.levelReason: N5 past-clause noun description and past nominal predicate; no Japanese N4 cost construction is required by the prompt or base choices.
